blogs.title: Goodbye Tokenizers: How the Byte Latent Transformer is Rewriting the Rules of LLMs
blogs.description: An accessible overview of the limitations of traditional tokenization in large language models. This post will explore how the Byte Latent Transformer (BLT) learns directly from raw bytes, solving long-standing issues like multilingual inequity, domain sensitivity, and fragility to input noise.

blogs.title: Smart Compute Allocation: The Magic Behind BLT's Dynamic Patching
blogs.description: A deep dive into BLT's unique architecture. This post will explain how the model uses a small byte-level language model to measure entropy and dynamically group bytes into 'patches,' ensuring that compute power is spent only on complex, unpredictable data rather than wasted on easy predictions.

blogs.title: Doing More with Less: How BLT Cuts LLM Inference Costs by Up to 50%
blogs.description: An exploration of BLT's incredible efficiency. This post will break down the paper's scaling studies, showing how BLT matches the performance of state-of-the-art models like Llama 3 while simultaneously scaling up model and patch sizes to slash inference compute costs by half.

blogs.title: Spelling Mistaakes? No Problem: Why Byte-Level LLMs are More Robust
blogs.description: A look at BLT's superior handling of character-level tasks, noisy inputs, and low-resource languages. This post will highlight how bypassing fixed tokenizers gives the model a fundamental, human-like understanding of spelling, phonology, and text manipulation.

blogs.title: From Llama 3 to BLT: How to 'Byte-ify' Your Existing Language Models
blogs.description: A practical look at the paper's proposal for transitioning existing models to the new architecture. This post will explain how researchers can initialize a BLT model using pre-trained weights from traditional token-based models like Llama 3, offering a faster, more compute-efficient path to tokenizer-free AI.
